title: NFL Confirms Super Bowl LXII in Atlanta for February 13, 2028, Locking 17-Game Schedule Through 2027
dek: The NFL finalized Super Bowl LXII for February 13, 2028, in Atlanta, effectively confirming the 2027 season will run 17 games and pushing any 18-game expansion to no earlier than 2028. Team owners favor the expansion; the players union opposes it and formal bargaining has not begun.
author: The GoCheckMySports Desk
key_fact: The NFL set Super Bowl LXII for February 13, 2028, in Atlanta, locking the 2027 season into a 17-game schedule and delaying any 18-game season expansion to at least 2028.
bottom_line: The February 2028 Super Bowl date removes uncertainty for Atlanta and fixes the 2027 season at 17 games. What to watch is when formal bargaining between the league and the union begins and what concessions or conditions might move the union toward acceptance or trigger further delay.
body: The NFL finalized Super Bowl LXII for February 13, 2028, at Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta, according to Front Office Sports. The date confirmation effectively locks the 2027 season into a 17-game format and pushes any expansion to an 18-game season to no earlier than 2028.

The league had held multiple potential dates for the Super Bowl while deliberation on an enlarged regular season extended for nearly two years. Atlanta was awarded Super Bowl LXII in October 2024, but local officials and hospitality executives grew increasingly frustrated by their inability to advance planning without a confirmed game date. The 2026 season will also run 17 games, culminating with Super Bowl LXI at SoFi Stadium in California on February 14, 2027. The NFL has awarded Super Bowls for 2029 and 2030 to Las Vegas and Nashville, respectively.

The 18-game debate has divided the league and its players union. Many team owners, notably New England Patriots owner Robert Kraft, have openly advocated for the expansion, which the league views as a vehicle to advance its international ambitions. The NFL Players Association, however, has been openly resistant to an 18-game season. Formal bargaining between the league and the union on the topic has not yet begun. The union appointed JC Tretter as executive director in March. In statements earlier this year, NFL Commissioner Roger Goodell indicated an 18-game season was not "a given," signaling a more cautious public stance on the topic than some owners have taken.
The Super Bowl date effectively forces the earliest possible window for an 18-game debut to the 2028 season, contingent on labor agreement.
